# zrotg

> Constructs a complex Givens plane rotation.

<section class="intro">

On exit, `a` is overwritten with the rotated value `r`, `c` holds the real cosine, and `s` holds the complex sine.

</section>

<!-- /.intro -->

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import zrotg from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/zrotg';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
zrotg( a, b, c, s ) → void
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `a` | `Complex128Array` | **in/out** · On entry, complex scalar `a`; on exit, overwritten with `r` |
| `b` | `Complex128Array` | Complex scalar `b` (input only) |
| `c` | `Float64Array` | **out** · On exit, the real cosine of the rotation |
| `s` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · On exit, the complex sine of the rotation |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `a`: On entry, the scalar a. On exit, the scalar r.
- `b`: The scalar b.
- `c`: The scalar c.
- `s`: The scalar s.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
zrotg.strided( a, offsetA, b, offsetB, c, offsetC, s, offsetS ) → void
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `a` | `Complex128Array` | **in/out** · On entry, complex scalar `a`; on exit, overwritten with `r` |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Index offset for `a` (in complex elements) |
| `b` | `Complex128Array` | Complex scalar `b` (input only) |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Index offset for `b` (in complex elements) |
| `c` | `Float64Array` | **out** · On exit, the real cosine of the rotation |
| ↳ `offsetC` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Index offset for `c` |
| `s` | `Complex128Array` | **out** · On exit, the complex sine of the rotation |
| ↳ `offsetS` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Index offset for `s` (in complex elements) |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `a`: On entry, the scalar a. On exit, the scalar r.
- `b`: The scalar b.
- `c`: The scalar c.
- `s`: The scalar s.

</details>

**Returns** `void`

</section>

## Notes

-   `zrotg()` corresponds to the reference BLAS routine [`ZROTG`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/BLAS/SRC/zrotg.f90).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import Complex128Array from '@stdlib/array/complex128/lib/index.js';
import reinterpret from '@stdlib/strided/base/reinterpret-complex128/lib/index.js';
import zrotg from '@rreusser/blahpack/blas/zrotg';

// Generate a complex Givens rotation which zeros `b` in [ a; b ] = [ 3; 4 ]:

// Using the standard interface:
let a = new Complex128Array( [ 3.0, 0.0 ] );
let b = new Complex128Array( [ 4.0, 0.0 ] );
let c = new Float64Array( 1 );
let s = new Complex128Array( 1 );
zrotg( a, b, c, s );
console.log( reinterpret( a, 0 ), c, reinterpret( s, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => r = 5, c = 0.6, s = 0.8

// Using the strided interface:
a = new Complex128Array( [ 3.0, 0.0 ] );
b = new Complex128Array( [ 4.0, 0.0 ] );
c = new Float64Array( 1 );
s = new Complex128Array( 1 );
zrotg.strided( a, 0, b, 0, c, 0, s, 0 );
console.log( reinterpret( a, 0 ), c, reinterpret( s, 0 ) ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference BLAS 3.12.0 source of `ZROTG`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

ZROTG constructs a plane rotation

$$
\begin{bmatrix} c & s \\ -\overline{s} & c \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} a \\ b \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} r \\ 0 \end{bmatrix}
$$

where c is real, s is complex, and $c^2 + \overline{s} \, s = 1$.

The computation uses the formulas

```text
   |x| = sqrt( Re(x)**2 + Im(x)**2 )
   sgn(x) = x / |x|  if x /= 0
          = 1        if x  = 0
   c = |a| / sqrt(|a|**2 + |b|**2)
   s = sgn(a) * conjg(b) / sqrt(|a|**2 + |b|**2)
   r = sgn(a)*sqrt(|a|**2 + |b|**2)
When a and b are real and r /= 0, the formulas simplify to
   c = a / r
   s = b / r
```

the same as in DROTG when \|a\| \> \|b\|. When \|b\| \>= \|a\|, the sign of c and s will be different from those computed by DROTG if the signs of a and b are not the same.

### Further Details

Based on the algorithm from

Anderson E. (2017) Algorithm 978: Safe Scaling in the Level 1 BLAS ACM Trans Math Softw 44:1--28 https://doi.org/10.1145/3061665

</section>

<!-- /.reference-notes -->
